instruction: Check that campground-related elements are visible to validate successful loading of the recreation.gov campground page.

metadata.explanation: Task variation 4: Verify the recreation.gov page has loaded correctly by checking for campground-related CSS class elements. This variation is similar to the original in that it parses HTML content to verify page elements, but instead of checking for a specific booking table header, it checks for the presence of any elements with 'camp' in their class names, which is common on recreation.gov pages. This maintains similar complexity and interaction pattern as the original task.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies recreation.gov page loaded with multiple checks: domain validation, search buttons, booking elements, recreation logo, campground content, and page title
Getter uses Playwright selectors which are appropriate for modern SPA sites like recreation.gov
Getter waits for JavaScript rendering (2 second timeout) before checking elements
Multi-level verification with 6 different checks requiring at least 3 to pass provides robust validation
Domain check ensures page is on recreation.gov before verifying content
Metric correctly validates is_recreation_domain flag and minimum checks passed threshold
Minor issue: Metric hardcodes minimum checks (3) and domain requirement instead of using expected.min_checks_passed and expected.require_recreation_domain from rules
Minor issue: expected.has_elements field is checked but not meaningfully used in validation logic (backward compatibility field)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Update metric chrome.py:58 to use expected.get('min_checks_passed', 3) instead of hardcoded 3
Update metric chrome.py:54 to use expected.get('require_recreation_domain', True) for conditional domain checking
Consider removing or documenting the 'has_elements' field as it appears to be for backward compatibility only
